text:
A: Hello! Oh, there you are. Can you hear me? I'm never sure with these laptops.
B: Yeah, I can hear you.
A: Good, good. I'm Marijke. Don't worry about the accent, I'm Dutch, but I've been in Kent forty years so it's all mixed up now. And I think I'm the oldest one here, so be patient with me.
B: It's fine. I'm Callum. Stockton.
A: Stockton, that's up north, isn't it? Near Middlesbrough?
B: Yeah, next to it.
A: Never been. Furthest north I've been is, erm, York maybe, on a coach trip. So what do you do, Callum?
B: Student. Final year, civil engineering at Teesside.
A: Oh, engineering, very clever. Bridges and that?
B: Sometimes. I'm mostly doing drainage. My dissertation's on drainage for new housing estates, like where the rainwater goes so the houses don't flood.
A: Well, that's important. They're building all these new estates round us in Sittingbourne and half the gardens are like a swamp. My friend's in one, she's got a puddle you could keep ducks in.
B: Yeah, that's usually the soakaways. Clay ground, they don't drain properly. Or someone's cut corners on the design.
A: There you go, you should go and tell them.
B: Maybe.
A: I'm a carer. Morning calls, washing, dressing, breakfast, make sure they take their tablets. Just part-time now, twelve hours. I finish by eleven and then the day is mine.
B: My mam's a care assistant. In a home, though.
A: Oh, is she? Then she knows. It's hard on the body. My knees, I tell you, some of these houses have stairs like a lighthouse. And the parking, honestly, in the cul-de-sacs I go round and round. Last week I had to park by the shops and walk, and the lady I go to, she's ninety-one, she says, you're late, Marijke, and I say yes, I know, blame the man with the van. She's lovely, she just likes her porridge at half eight.
B: Mam says the same about her back.
A: Everybody does. Do you live at home then?
B: Yeah. Saves on rent. I do Saturdays at Morrisons as well, so.
A: Very sensible. My son was the same, he stayed home till he was twenty-six, I couldn't get rid of him. Did you do that puzzle at the start? I was useless.
B: It was alright. Last one was a bit awkward.
A: Awkward! I was just pressing buttons. Keith, my husband, came in and said what are you doing, and I said I don't know, it's research.
B: Fair enough.
A: So what are you going to do after? Building things?
B: Hopefully a graduate job round here. Drainage or highways. Then work towards chartership, then save for a house.
A: You've got it all planned. Good for you. I never planned anything. I came on a coach holiday, met Keith, and that was that.
B: That's a bit different.
A: Ha, a little bit. What else, erm... do you do anything for fun, or is it all books?
B: Gym mostly. Watch the Boro with my stepdad.
A: Keith's football mad as well. All weekend, the telly. I just sit with my word search.
B: Yeah. That's about it really.
A: Well, it's been nice. I think that's our time nearly.
